proposal: The Mandate says State should move beyond non-binding, informal standards of cyberspace behavior and work with allies to establish a clear framework of enforceable norms beyond the voluntary UN Group of Governmental Experts norms, should assist the Department of Defense to go on offense against adversaries below the level of armed conflict, and should work with allies and engage adversaries to draw clear lines of unacceptable conduct (pages 195 and 196).
remaining: A framework of enforceable cyberspace norms agreed with allies, beyond the voluntary UN norms (page 196; none found)
A stated State Department role in assisting DOD offensive operations below the level of armed conflict (page 196; the strategy does not name State)
Engagement with allies and adversaries to draw clear lines of unacceptable conduct (page 196; EO 14390 addresses only cybercrime and fraud)

status_summary: On 2026-03-06 the White House released President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America, which commits to defensive and offensive cyber operations, to using all instruments of national power to raise adversaries' costs, and to engaging internationally so that norms and standards reflect US values, but it names neither enforceable norms nor a State Department role. The same day Executive Order 14390 directed the Secretary of State to press foreign governments to act against cybercrime and fraud networks and to coordinate with allies on consequences, such as sanctions and visa restrictions, for states that tolerate them. No allied framework of enforceable cyberspace norms was found.

timeline.event: The White House released President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America, committing to defensive and offensive cyber operations, to raising adversaries' costs with all instruments of national power, and to international engagement so that norms reflect US values.

Executive Order 14390, Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens, was signed, directing the Secretary of State to engage foreign governments, coordinate with allies and consider sanctions, visa restrictions and other consequences for states that tolerate cybercrime groups.

title: Cyber diplomacy: enforceable norms with allies and help DOD go on offense below conflict
uncertainties: The strategy was read through a fetch summary, not page by page, so a passage on norms or State could have been missed. The Pall Mall Process, any allied binding framework, the offensive-cyber presidential memorandum and a reported offensive cyber appropriation were not confirmed. An advocacy group's explainer reports that the UN General Assembly established a non-binding Global Mechanism on ICT security on 2025-12-01 after the open-ended working group's July 2025 report; this is a UN action and is not a timeline event. A news site reported on 2025-04-22 that State's reorganization moved the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy under the Economic Growth office; the effective date and current placement were not confirmed, so it is not a timeline event. Searches on the US position at the UN mechanism returned no US statement.
